posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Playing around for the most part but this hologram came out just about as I'd envisioned.

![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/gallery/d/4172-1/4th2color.jpg)

The colors in the photo aren't precisely true as the red is deeper and the flag is green in real-life.

Double exposure with the film TEA treated 4% for the flag and washed out for the fireworks.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Michael, that is superb!! Really!!! I like it!!!

How did you create the object of the fireworks?

Why do you pretreat first, dry, then wash out and have to dry again to do the second exposure. Wouldn't it be easier to do the first exposure (red fireworks) then treat with TEA and dry, then shoot flay and just process?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Michael, that is superb!! Really!!! I like it!!!

Thanks. I'm really happy with it too.

> **JohnFP:** How did you create the object of the fireworks?

Paint and glass. There's more information in my original post [over here](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?p=36782#36782)

> **JohnFP:** Why do you pretreat first, dry, then wash out and have to dry again to do the second exposure. Wouldn't it be easier to do the first exposure (red fireworks) then treat with TEA and dry, then shoot flay and just process?

I did it that way partly because my film was already treated for green (I tend to do it in small batches so I don't have to wait every time I want to shoot).

Even if I'd been starting fresh I would have at least treated the fireworks just to shorten the exposure time. So either way, there'd be two trips through liquid before I developed the film. So the overall process is: TEA treat, dry, shoot, wash out TEA, dry, shoot, soak in water, develop etc.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Cool! Did you have to adjust beam angles for each exposure to compensate for the different reconstruction wavelengths or was the image alignment close enough (for this subject) without adjustment?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **Tom B.:** Cool! Did you have to adjust beam angles for each exposure to compensate for the different reconstruction wavelengths or was the image alignment close enough (for this subject) without adjustment?

It's difficult to tell if the images are out of alignment because the "master" for the fireworks was only 2" tall (it was really only intended to be a test shot) while the master for the flag was 5". The fireworks come in slightly before the flag when moving up and down but I think the overall effect works well for this subject.

I'm definitely going to have to keep angles and height in mind for the other 2-color holograms I'm working on though.

btw, I've updated the image to show the final matting and framing.
